One of the most frustrating parts of the persona community is the weird aversion to playing the games. One of the most popular inside jokes in the community is that “Persona fans don’t play their own games,” though slowly this has gone from a punchline to a mantra that’s being upheld. I’m certainly not the first person to notice this, but it’s a trend that I've seen become more common as time goes on. While it’s easy to point and laugh at these people, lately I’ve been wondering the reason WHY this option is so appealing. If you’re watching this video, then there’s a very high chance that you view video games as art. MePersona is the AI-powered workspace built for content creators who are stretched across too many platforms at once. It maps your real voice from a short audio sample, then helps you reply to fans, organize your content, and post on schedule — everywhere you're active — while still sounding unmistakably like you. At the center is your AI persona: trained i n minutes, it learns how you talk, write, and post. From there, MePersona pulls fan messages from across your platforms into one unified inbox, drafts voice-matched replies for you to approve, keeps an auto-organized content vault, and runs a marketing agent that plans campaigns in your voice. Nothing goes out without your sign-off — every AI-drafted reply, post, and campaign passes through a review queue you control. MePersona works [...] passes through a review queue you control. MePersona works across X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Telegram, Patreon, Discord, LinkedIn, and Bluesky, with more on the way. And because your persona isn't locked inside the app, the Persona API lets you connect it to the tools you already use — from automation workflows to your own website. MePersona was built on a simple idea: creators shouldn't have to choose between showing up everywhere and sounding like themselves.
